title: How Hot the Knees Get: Torque Over a Step, the Heat of the Windings, and How Heavy a Robot the Legs Can Carry

questions.question: Why does a trot heat the knees more than standing?
options: The legs swing faster, and the swing is what heats them
The body is higher in a trot
The servos are less efficient at a trot's pace
Only two feet are down, so each carries twice the load and heat goes as the square
questions.explanation: Two feet share the weight where four did, so the stance torque doubles and the heat while it is on quadruples: 28.1 K against 14.0 K.

questions.question: The knee's stance torque in the trot was:
questions.explanation: Standing on four feet the knee gave 4.33 N m; with two down it carries twice the load. 6.12 N m is the rms over the cycle, swing included.

questions.question: Which torque sets the heating over a cycle?
options: The largest torque in the cycle
The root mean square
The average torque over the cycle
The torque in the stance alone
questions.explanation: Heat goes as the square of the current, so the squares are averaged and then rooted. In the trot that gave 6.12 N m from 8.65 in the stance and 0.3 in the swing.

questions.question: The heaviest body the knees could trot with at 0.30 m:
options: 12 kg, what it was built for
35 kg, twice the trot's figure
40 kg, the robot of the crouch test
questions.explanation: By halving an interval, the heaviest body whose knees settle at or under the 60 K limit. Crouched lower the figure is much less.

questions.question: What happens to a heavy robot held in a crouch?
options: The windings pass their limit in time, here 25 s, and the legs go limp
It settles at a temperature under the limit, as any pose does
The battery runs down before the knees warm
The torque falls as the windings heat, so it sinks slowly
questions.explanation: A pose whose settling temperature is over the limit can only be held for a time. The 40 kg robot crouched on four feet had 25 s.

questions.question: What is not in this model?
options: The swing's small torque
The number of feet on the ground
Impact peaks at touchdown, and the controller that cuts current
The thermal resistance of the motor
questions.explanation: The model is one lump of heat and a steady cycle. The jolt of each landing, and a drive that cuts the current when hot, are not in it.
